source_title: Received Jio allotment? Here's how much money you can make on listing day - India Today
source_excerpt:
Jio Platforms IPO allottees are assessing potential returns before the October 28 market debut. The latest Rs 246 grey market premium indicates an estimated listing gain of nearly 22%.
Jio Platforms IPO investors who have received shares in the allotment may be looking at potential listing gains of nearly 22%, based on the latest grey market premium (GMP). With the company's shares scheduled to list on October 28, investors are now watching whether the stock can deliver gains in line with grey market expectations.
The Jio Platforms IPO 's latest recorded GMP stood at Rs 246 as of 9:37 am on October 27, 2026, according to the data available. Against the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 1,119 per share, this implies an estimated listing price of Rs 1,365.
At this price, the expected listing gain works out to around 21.98% over the issue price. However, GMP is an unofficial indicator of market sentiment and does not guarantee the actual listing price or returns investors will make. HOW MUCH CAN JIO IPO INVESTORS MAKE?
The Jio Platforms IPO had a lot size of 12 shares, with the issue priced at Rs 1,119 per share at the upper end of the price band. An investor allotted one lot would have invested Rs 13,428.
Based on the current GMP of Rs 246 per share, an investor holding one lot could make an estimated listing gain of Rs 2,952 . At the implied listing price of Rs 1,365, the total value of the 12 shares would be Rs 16,380.
For an investor allotted two lots, comprising 24 shares, the investment would be Rs 26,856. At the current GMP, the estimated gain would be Rs 5,904, taking the total value of the holding to Rs 32,760.
An investor who received three lots, or 36 shares, would have invested Rs 40,284. If the shares list at the estimated price of Rs 1,365, the holding would be worth Rs 49,140, implying a gain of Rs 8,856.
For investors allotted five lots, comprising 60 shares, the investment would be Rs 67,140. Based on the current GMP, the estimated listing gain would be Rs 14,760, taking the total value of the shares to Rs 81,900.
These calculations are indicative and assume that the shares list at Rs 1,365. Actual gains or losses will depend on the listing price and subsequent market movements. Brokerage charges, taxes and other applicable costs have not been included. HOW TO CHECK JIO PLATFORMS IPO ALLOTMENT STATUS
HOW TO CHECK JIO PLATFORMS IPO ALLOTMENT STATUS
Investors can check their allotment status through KFin Technologies, the registrar to the issue, or through the BSE and NSE websites.
To check the status on KFin Technologies, visit their website and select Jio Platforms from the IPO list. Choose the relevant search option, such as PAN, application number or demat account number, enter the required details and submit them to view the allotment status.
On the BSE website , select 'Equity' under the issue type, choose Jio Platforms from the issue name list, enter your PAN or application number, complete the verification process and submit the details.
Investors can also check the available IPO bid details through the NSE website by clicking here .
Select 'Equity & SME IPO bid details', choose Jio Platforms from the symbol list, enter the required details and submit the request.
The allotment status will show whether shares have been allotted and, where applicable, the number of shares received. Investors should use the official registrar and exchange websites to confirm their status. WHEN WILL JIO PLATFORMS SHARES LIST?
Jio Platforms shares are scheduled to list on the BSE and NSE on October 28, 2026. The IPO was open for subscription from October 21 to October 23, with a price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share and a lot size of 12 shares.
The issue attracted an overall subscription of 22.19 times. The registrar is KFin Technologies, while Kotak Mahindra Capital Company is the book-running lead manager.
While the GMP points to a potential listing gain of around 22%, investors will get a clearer picture of the stock's market value once trading begins. The actual listing price could be higher or lower than the estimate implied by the grey market. - Ends
